Write and read a subclass's payload in a definition file

Source: R/definition.R
scale_payload_io.Rd

The seam a dimension package uses to carry what the core does not know about – geoscales' geometry – in a scale definition written by write_scale() and read by read_scale().

Usage

scale_write_payload(x, ...)

scale_read_payload(x, ...)

register_scale_class(class)

list_scale_classes()

Arguments

x

A NestedScale (the subclass instance when writing; the core object when reading).

...

Method arguments: dir, the bundle directory or NULL, and header, the header list.

class

An S7 class that inherits from scale_class().

Value

scale_write_payload() the header; scale_read_payload() a scale; register_scale_class() the registry key, invisibly; list_scale_classes() a character vector of registered class names.

Details

scale_write_payload(x, dir, header) is called after the core tables are written, with the bundle directory (NULL for a single-file definition, which can hold inline data only) and the header so far; it writes its files and returns the header with its entries added under payload. scale_read_payload(x, dir, header) is called with the CORE scale rebuilt from the header and returns the subclass object. The NestedScale defaults return the header and x unchanged.

read_scale() finds the method through the class recorded in the header, so a dimension package registers its class once, in .onLoad(), with register_scale_class().

Examples

list_scale_classes()
#> character(0)
